title: Radio: Topeka Depot to Duty Desk, Boom ETA and Tier 2

fields.centerName: Cooperative Duty Desk (relayed to Ironbark QI line)

lines.text: Duty desk, Topeka depot. We got the activation page at 06:48. One crew is loading the trailer now. Three thousand feet of 18-inch river boom, two skimmers, two shallow-draft boats. If we're rolling by 07:30, I can have the first boom at the Mill Ridge ramp around 10:20.

Okay. Wichita says they have 2,500 feet ready but no driver until 08:00. Kansas City has 4,000 feet and six boats, but the subcontractor dispatcher says he can't put crews on those boats for at least four hours unless somebody calls Tier 2 now.

One more thing. Your Ironbark ops chief phoned me directly and wants the boom strung straight across the river at the ramp. At 2 knots that boom just passes oil underneath it. So who's giving me the boom sites, and is Tier 2 a go? Topeka depot, standing by.

fields.voiceStyle: Male in his forties, practical field lead, brisk and a little impatient, a forklift working nearby, raising his voice slightly over the depot noise

instructorNote: Purpose: show the OSRO arrival time against how fast the oil is moving, push a Tier 2 decision, and test who sets boom sites. Once the audio ends, read aloud the line from the Ironbark room: "Three and a half hours? The oil passes the ramp before then." Watch for: the OSRO logs 06:48 as the activation time and calls Tier 2 and the subcontractors now; the OSRO refuses boom set square across the river and plans deflection at about 15 degrees toward bank recovery pockets (Cooperative plan section 4); the QI confirms funding, records the activation in the notification log, and sends boom-site priorities through Unified Command and the ICS 202. The QI should accept that the ramp is already lost and put the mile 9.5 deflection site and the mile 11 intake first.
